body:
## Purpose

This PR turns spectral element operators into ordinary broadcast expressions built on the loop primitives from #2522, completing the second task outlined in #2468. A `SpectralBroadcasted` is now just a `Broadcasted` whose function is a `SpectralElementOperator`, so spectral operators compose with pointwise broadcasts, run through the same scope-dispatched `foreach_slice` machinery on CPUs and GPUs, and no longer need hand-written CUDA kernels.

## Disclosure

The second commit in this PR was generated using Claude. The PR description was also partially generated by Claude.

## Content

- Rewrite `SpectralElementOperator`s as slab-wise applications of the DataLayouts loop primitives
  - `SpectralBroadcasted` is now `Broadcasted{SpectralStyle}`; each operator is an `apply_operator(op, args...)` on one slab, driven by `foreach_slab` — one fused loop on CPUs, one kernel launch on GPUs, replacing `ext/cuda/operators_spectral_element.jl` and `ext/cuda/operators_sem_shmem.jl`
  - Weak-form operators are parameterizations of the strong-form ones (e.g. `Divergence{WeakForm}`), with `WeakDivergence` etc. as deprecated aliases; `NEWS.md` records the interface changes
  - Shape queries replace operator nodes with constants of their result eltypes (`drop_operators`), which keeps the mutually recursive queries below Julia's recursion limiter inside fused kernels
- Support spectral operators in fused loop bodies
  - Later statements may read earlier results, both pointwise and through operators; cross-statement spectral reads publish through synchronized shared buffers
  - In-body temporaries live in per-thread registers, so they stay live across later spectral statements instead of aliasing the equal-size shared operator buffers; `Restrict` cannot read a register-resident argument and throws a descriptive error
  - `Utilities.@drop_recursion_limits` and `Utilities.@drop_constprop` centralize the `Method`-level inference controls, covering `Core.kwcall` methods and their hidden body functions, where keyword arguments put the loop bodies
  - A Tuple-only `Utilities.Unrolled.unrolled_tuple_map` carries the hot broadcast-tree walks (about a tenth of a spectral expression's compilation memory); `UnrolledUtilities` imports are unchanged from `main`
- Keep shared memory unaliased and the launch configuration consistent with the slice loops
  - Operator destinations live in per-thread registers; shared-memory globals are named by byte size, since same-named globals from separately compiled functions resolve to one
  - Every sub-block wider than a warp gets a block of its own, so a block barrier is the sub-block's barrier and no sub-block indexes another's shared memory
  - Per-thread index arithmetic stays off the device (no emulated integer division), operator applications inline below a bounded buffer size, and constant propagation is disabled on host-side loop entries only (kernel-side constprop shifts the sm_60 register brink)
- Tighten the slicing APIs to fail loudly: generic `level`/`slab`/`column` fallbacks are narrowed, `todata` is replaced by `field_values`, and a sliced broadcast mixing level and extruded fields recomputes its axes correctly
- Fix a preexisting bug from #2602: `ext/cuda/operators_dg.jl` called `CUDA.CuStaticSharedArray` directly, giving a 512-byte and a 256-byte buffer the same global
- Tests and CI
  - Fused-loop testsets cover in-place destinations, destinations as inputs, and register-resident temporaries read across later spectral statements, against unfused references for every space; plus zero-allocation gates, multi-warp slabs, and shared-memory naming assertions
  - The divergence compiler stress test pins the register brink from both sides (12 operators compile, 24 fail on sm_60); a temporary probe in the next build locates the exact brink
  - Coverage instrumentation multiplies LLVM time on large fused kernels, so the fusion testsets skip under coverage and `Spectral elem - rectilinear` is `slow`-tiered (GHA excludes it; Buildkite runs it uninstrumented); several other tests with large inference allocation increases are also `slow`-tiered to avoid OOM kills on 16 GB Github Actions runners

## Roadmap

A suggested order for reviewing the changes:

1. **Operator rewrite** — the bulk of the PR:
   `src/Operators/spectralelement.jl`, `src/Operators/common.jl`, `src/Operators/deprecated.jl`, `src/Geometry/conversions.jl`
2. **Register-resident destinations and scopes**:
   `src/DataLayouts/registers.jl`, `src/DataLayouts/scopes.jl`, `src/DataLayouts/loops.jl`
3. **GPU launch, shared memory, and barriers**:
   `ext/cuda/scopes.jl`, `ext/cuda/loops.jl`, `ext/cuda/cuda_utils.jl`
4. **Slicing and broadcast plumbing**:
   `src/DataLayouts/indexing.jl`, `src/DataLayouts/struct_storage.jl`, `src/Fields/broadcast.jl`, `src/Fields/Fields.jl`, `src/Utilities/Utilities.jl`
5. **Preexisting `main` bugfix**:
   `ext/cuda/operators_dg.jl`, `src/Operators/numericalflux.jl`
6. **New and updated tests**:
   `test/Fields/unit_field.jl`, `test/DataLayouts/unit_loops.jl`, `test/Operators/spectralelement/allocs_spectral_ops.jl`, `test/Operators/spectralelement/gpu_rectilinear.jl`, `test/gpu/compiler_stress_regression.jl`, `perf/stress_test_compiler.jl`

## Performance Comparison

Baselines are the last pre-merge `main` builds ([7618](https://buildkite.com/clima/climacore-ci/builds/7618), [142](https://buildkite.com/clima/climaatmos-downstream/builds/142), [1476](https://buildkite.com/clima/climacoupler-coarse-nightly-amip/builds/1476)) against the merged head ([7650](https://buildkite.com/clima/climacore-ci/builds/7650), [172](https://buildkite.com/clima/climaatmos-downstream/builds/172), [1486](https://buildkite.com/clima/climacoupler-coarse-nightly-amip/builds/1486)). Job names and measurements are taken from the logs, with center-space layout dimensions `(v, i, j, h)` where available; each measurement links to its job. Noise floors come from repeated builds of this branch. **Positive Δ = slower or more memory on this branch.**

| Job | Logged measurement | `main` | This branch | Δ | Noise floor |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| `Flagship AMIP GPU with prognostic EDMF + 1M + integrated land (16 helems)` — (63, 4, 4, 1536) | "Built cache" (time, memory) | [227.053 s, 41.24 GiB](https://buildkite.com/clima/climacoupler-coarse-nightly-amip/builds/1476#01a04619-7141-48ce-ae11-de73c0cd41d4) | [215.673 s, 34.93 GiB](https://buildkite.com/clima/climacoupler-coarse-nightly-amip/builds/1486#01a059da-df38-4f9e-af8d-4a4ee4d1f017) | **−5.0%, −15.3%** | ±5% |

| `stretched 2D plane inertial gravity wave` — (20, 2, 1, 300) | job wall time | [13.2 min](https://buildkite.com/clima/climacore-ci/builds/7618#01a04acd-637e-4b40-b5fa-60d392ff5355) | [9.8 min](https://buildkite.com/clima/climacore-ci/builds/7650#01a05a2e-28d0-4fad-90dd-f7be8becf713) | **−26%** | ±11% |
| ClimaCore CI / ClimaAtmos downstream, jobs > 1 min passed in both builds (146 / 83) | summed job wall time | [12.8 h](https://buildkite.com/clima/climacore-ci/builds/7618) / [24.3 h](https://buildkite.com/clima/climaatmos-downstream/builds/142) | [13.7 h](https://buildkite.com/clima/climacore-ci/builds/7650) / [25.6 h](https://buildkite.com/clima/climaatmos-downstream/builds/172) | **+7% / +6%** | ±3% |

Note on build [1486](https://buildkite.com/clima/climacoupler-coarse-nightly-amip/builds/1486): the coarse one-moment microphysics AMIP job crashed following CliMA/ClimaAtmos.jl#4793; not related to this PR.

The GPU costs share one cause: work a CPU pays once per slice, a GPU pays once per thread. Compilation is slowed down and inference allocations are up because fusing operators into one kernel means one larger inference problem instead of several small ones.

## Lessons Learned

- **Shared-memory globals are keyed by name, not by allocation site.** `CUDA.CuStaticSharedArray` emits every allocation as an LLVM global literally named `shmem`; two such globals from *different method instances* resolve to one, regardless of size, so a 4096-byte buffer can silently run on a 2048-byte global. Two allocations inside the same method instance are guaranteed to be unique. Any future kernel that allocates shared memory must go through `scoped_static_array`, which encodes the byte size in the name.
- **`@noinline` on a device function is expensive.** An `@noinline` operator application becomes an NVPTX device call with byval/sret stack buffers — about 1.5 KB of per-thread local traffic for a kernel doing ~19 flops per thread. It is also what makes cross-application buffer reuse possible, so the two are coupled: inlining removes the aliasing hazard but grows shared memory per block.
- **`constprop = 0x02` is worth reaching for when a function is re-inferred per constant argument.** The spectral entry points take singleton form types and dimension `Val`s, and constant propagation could never change their answers because every dispatch is on a type. Disabling it cut inference allocation by 26% and left runtime unchanged.
title: Enable fusion of spectral element operators

body:
## Summary

Stacked on top of #2598.

This PR introduces GPU performance optimizations targeting large-scale cubed-sphere simulations (evaluated on an NVIDIA A100 with $h_\text{elem}=30, z_\text{elem}=63$), plus horizontal Laplacian atoms that centralize the hyperdiffusion pattern:

1. **Flattened `FieldVector` broadcasts on GPU** (the bulk of the speedup):
   - When every array in a `FieldVector` broadcast has the same contiguous layout as the destination, the expression is evaluated over `vec`s of the arrays with plain linear indexing, bypassing CUDA.jl's N-dimensional Cartesian index computation (4 sequential integer divisions/modulos per thread for these 4-D arrays). Vector update bandwidth reached **1.31 TB/s** (**3.04× faster per update**).
   - In-place updates like `x .-= dx` preserve destination object identity through the flattening, so `Base.Broadcast`'s aliasing check no longer allocates a defensive copy of the destination on every stage update — previously **7.85 GB of device allocations per step** on the 63-level sphere; time-step integration is now zero-allocation, worth another ~5% per step (241.0 → 228.2 ms).
   - The GPU extension marks its array types via a `Fields.is_gpu_array_type` trait (SubArrays recurse into their parent type); CPU broadcasts keep the standard path unchanged. Unit-tested: the gate, the transform, the destination-identity invariant, aliased in-place updates, and the end-to-end `FieldVector` broadcast (which exercises the flattened path on GPU CI).
2. **Horizontal Laplacian atoms + overlapped intermediate DSS in hyperdiffusion:**
   - Adds `Operators.scalar_laplacian` and `Operators.vector_laplacian`, the building blocks of ∇⁴ hyperdiffusion. On CG spaces they return lazy, element-local operator expressions that fuse into consuming broadcasts; on DG spaces `scalar_laplacian` includes the interior-penalty face corrections itself and `weighted_dss!` is a no-op, so one prep → `weighted_dss!` → apply sequence serves both discretizations.
   - The hybrid example's `hyperdiffusion_tendency!` is rewritten on the atoms: both intermediate Laplacians are computed before a single `Spaces.weighted_dss!(ᶜχ => ..., ᶜχuₕ => ...)` call, batching the scalar and vector exchanges into one communication phase, and the 2D/3D branching disappears into the atoms.
3. **Launch configuration & occupancy tuning:**
   - Capped `MAX_SUBBLOCK_LAUNCH_THREADS = 128` (4 warps/block) for 2D spectral slabs, halving shared-memory allocation per block to allow higher concurrent block occupancy per SM on large meshes.
   - Eager FD launch configurations pack 2 columns per block (128 threads) instead of 256, reducing register pressure, and query the SM count from the device instead of hardcoding the A100's 108.
   - The launch-configuration search keeps its **single-wave default** for now: with the allocation fix in place, a realistic-problem sweep found 4–8 waves ~6% faster per step (215 vs 228 ms), but the previously measured reduction slowdown at higher wave counts is unresolved, so the safest setting stands pending broader validation.
   - `CLIMA_CUDA_MAX_WAVES`, `CLIMA_FD_MAX_THREADS`, `CLIMA_DSS_MAX_THREADS`, and `CLIMA_COLLECT_KERNEL_STATS` environment variables (read once at module load into `Ref`s, never on the launch path) override the defaults; `perf/sweep_kernel_configs.jl` sweeps them on a benchmark case.
4. **Coalesced DG face-kernel memory access:**
   - Reshaped the DG staging buffer and `DGConnectivity` surface geometry to level-first layouts (`(Nv, Nq, nsides, nfaces)` and `(Nv, Nq, nfaces)`) and reordered thread indexing in the interior, boundary, ghost-face, and pack kernels to `(v, q, f)`, so warp threads share the face-node indices derived from `(q, f)` and read fields, geometry, and staging in contiguous 128-byte transactions; face kernels run in 128-thread blocks (`DG_FACE_BLOCK_THREADS`). Face flux evaluation is **1.72× faster**, accelerating DG flux computations by ~30% overall.

---

## Performance Metrics

*Benchmark: Baroclinic wave (`sphere/baroclinic_wave_rhoe`), $h_\text{elem}=30, z_\text{elem}=63$, $N_q=5$ (sweeps at $N_q=4$), $dt=400\,\text{s}$, NVIDIA A100 (40 GB SXM4).*

| Configuration | Median Step Time | Min Step Time | SYPD (Median) | SYPD (Max) | Speedup |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **Baseline (#2598)** | 293.6 ms | 291.8 ms | 3.73 | 3.75 | Baseline |
| **+ FieldVector 1D Flattening** | 238.0 ms | 237.3 ms | 4.60 | 4.62 | +23.4% |
| **+ Overlapped DSS & Tuning** | 237.5 ms | 237.1 ms | 4.615 | 4.622 | +23.7% |
| **+ Aliasing fix (zero device allocs/step)** | **228.2 ms** | — | — | — | **+28.7%** |

- The DG face-kernel coalescing (item 4) does not affect this CG benchmark; its 1.72× face-flux speedup was measured on the DG unit benchmarks.
- With the experimental `CLIMA_CUDA_MAX_WAVES=8` override, the same case reaches 214.9 ms/step (see the sweep results in the commit messages).

Co-produced with Gemini and Claude.
title: GPU performance optimizations

Stacked on top of #2606.

## Summary

Reduces ClimaCore's compilation latency. Profiling showed ~81% of initial space-creation time was Julia type inference over the grid/space constructors and operator broadcasts; this PR caches that work at package precompilation time and restructures the largest constructor.

*Note: based on #2606 (`ts/perf`); only the last two commits are new.*

1. **Precompilation workload** (`src/precompile_workload.jl`, no new dependencies): exercises small Float32/Float64 instances of interval meshes and FD spaces, cubed-sphere spectral-element grids, extruded center/face spaces, coordinate fields, scalar and covariant-vector broadcasts, the hyperdiffusion Laplaed, vector), continuous DSS, the common vertical

Reduces ClimaCore's first-use (TTFX) latency. Profiling showed ~81% of initial space-creation time was Julia type inference over the grid/space constructors and operator broadcasts; this PR caches that work at package precompilation time and restructures the largest constructor.

*Note: based on #2606 (`ts/perf`); only the last two commits are new.*

1. **Precompilation workload** (`src/precompile_workload.jl`, no new dependencies): exercises small Float32/Float64 instances of interval meshes and FD spaces, cubed-sphere spectral-nter/face spaces, coordinate fields, scalar andcovariant-vector broadcasts, the hyperdiffusion Laplacian atoms (scalar, weighted, vector), continuous DSS, the common vertical stencil operators, and FieldVector broadcasts (includdate). Guarded by the 1.10-compatible`ccall(:jl_generating_output, ...)`; `CLIMA_SKIP_PRECOMPILE_WORKLOAD=true` skips it during development. The global object cache is emptied afterwards so no workload objects are serialized into the package image.
2. **`_SpectralElementGrid2D` modularization**: the monolithic ~200-line constructor is split into `@noinline` units (`compute_nodal_local_geometries!`, `apply_bubble_correction!`, `compute_surface_geometries`), each inferred and cached separately. Also removes wasted work: the high-order quadrature area loop (4× the nodal evaluations) previously ran for every element even with
the bubble correction disabled, its result unused.

## Measurements

Representative downstream first use (fresh session, `z_elem = 10`, `h_elem = 4` — sizes *different* from the workload's):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Total (load + spaces + fields + operators) | 16.9 s (pre-workload) / 7.3 s | **4.5 s** |
| Scalar / vector spectral operator first use | 1.0 s / 2.3 s | 0.13 s / 0.35 s |
| At workload-matched sizes | — | fully cached (~0 s per operation) |

Package precompilation grows ~28 → ~32 s. No runtime code paths change (construction and broadcast results are bit-identical; sphere, bubble-correction, and allocation test tiers pass).

## Known limitation

`Nv`, `Ni`, `Nj` are static type parameters of the data layouts (only `Nh` is dynamic), so column-dependent code re-infers per new vertical extent — the remaining ~3 s at a novel `z_elem`, dominated by the extruded constructor's two `product_geometry` broadcasts (~1.2 s). The fix would be `Nv`-generic construction ayout variant); proposed as a follow-up item for #2605rather than attempted here.

Co-produced with Gemini and Claude
title: Reduce compilation time

body:
Stacked on #2607 (`ts/ttfx`).

Naming cleanup for the DG/spectral-element operators. No behavior change except
the rename of unexported names (no known downstream users, no shims).

- **`Operators.Outflow(; order = 0)`** — physically named convenience
  constructor returning `Extrapolate{order}()` (zero-normal-gradient outflow).
- **DG interior-face rename** `internal → interior`:
  `add_numerical_flux_interior!`, `add_lifting_flux_interior!`,
  `add_ldg_laplacian_flux_interior!` (and the CPU/CUDA device seams), plus the
  private grid field `internal_surface_geometry → interior_surface_geometry`.
- **`LeftBiased` → `BottomBiased` and `RightBiased` → `TopBiased`** (leaving 
   deprecation shims)
- **Weak-form aliases → parameterized form** repo-wide:
  `WeakDivergence()`/`WeakGradient()`/`WeakCurl()` →
  `Divergence{WeakForm}()`/`Gradient{WeakForm}()`/`Curl{WeakForm}()`. The
  aliases stay in `deprecated.jl` for downstream only.
- **Docs**: weak-form math folded into the `Divergence`/`Gradient`/`Curl`
  docstrings; `operators.md` documents the parameterized operators.
title: Naming cleanup for CG and DG operators
